title: Comparison for finite filtered page-two models
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $M$ be a functorial filtered-complex page-two model in $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-filtered-page-two-model], and let $f:U\to W$ be a morphism of filtered integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-sp-filtration]. Assume that both decreasing filtrations are finite. If every component of the induced map $E_2^{p,q}(f)$ is an isomorphism for all integers $p,q$, then $H^n(f)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $n$. No bound on the complex degrees is needed.

source.place: Tags 012K, 012Q, 012W and 015K: filtered-complex functoriality and finite-filtration convergence, together with Lemma 0127

proof.text: Propagate the page-two isomorphism to every page by integer induction. A componentwise page isomorphism is an isomorphism of complexes and induces homology isomorphisms; the spectral-sequence transition equation identifies the next-page map with their conjugate.

The quotient projection equation identifies the model quotient map with the actual canonical cokernel descent. Use the normalized canonical quotient-image isomorphism to compare the model page with the cycle/boundary cokernel. Extend its representative normalization from the representative subobject to actual cycles by factorization through that subobject and cancellation of cycle inclusions.

For fixed p and total degree n choose r beyond the common finite filtration bounds. The stationary cycle comparison identifies both page cokernels with the graded pieces of their cohomology-image filtrations and gives epimorphisms from actual cycles, normalized by their cohomology classes. The model naturality equation, homology functoriality, and the quotient-projection equations show that these actual-cycle epimorphisms intertwine the page map and the map on step cycles. Cancellation then identifies the graded cohomology map with the conjugate of the page isomorphism.

The cohomology-image filtrations are finite, since the original finite bounds also bound all degree steps. Apply finite-filtration induction to the filtered cohomology map, whose graded maps are the isomorphisms from the previous step. Its underlying map is H^n(f), as required. Zero objects, zero graded pieces, and any choices of finite bounds obey the same epi/mono cancellation arguments.
